I have farmed these 7 mu in Quzhou for 50 years. I am 69 now, finished middle school, then came straight back to the fields. My father taught me, and I learned the rest by doing it and watching the men around me whose families always eat well. I grow winter wheat and summer maize — same as everyone in this village. Last year my wheat made about 520 kg per mu and the maize about 580 kg. This year I will not change much. Change is risky, and I know this system.

For wheat, I will plant an improved variety — the dealer in town sells the same seed most of my neighbors buy, about 12 kg per mu, costs around 80 yuan. I will rotary till in October and spread one 50-kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base. That gives about 7 kg of phosphorus and 7 kg of potassium, plus some nitrogen. Then at green-up in March, I will top-dress with 20 kg of urea per mu. All together that is about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu. Yes, it is a bit heavy, but three years ago when I cut back to save money, the wheat turned yellow and thin, and I lost nearly 100 kg per mu. Never again. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. Electricity for the well pump is expensive, so I will irrigate three times: once before the deep freeze, once at jointing when the stems shoot up, and once when the grain is filling. I will spray twice — herbicide in early spring, then fungicide at heading because rust comes through some years. My wife helps with the spraying. For 7 mu we do not hire labor.

For maize, I will buy hybrid seed — 2.5 kg per mu. It is expensive, around 120 yuan per mu, but open-pollinated maize cannot compete anymore. Right after wheat harvest in early June, I will rotary till fast and plant. I will put down the same base fertilizer as wheat: one 50-kg bag of compound per mu. Then at the big trumpet stage, when the leaves are wide and the plant is hungry, I will追 25 kg of urea per mu. Maize needs more nitrogen than wheat if you want full ears, so that is about 20 kg nitrogen per mu total. I will irrigate twice from the well: once after sowing if the early summer drought hits, and once in August during grain filling if the rain does not come. Two sprays: herbicide after emergence, and one insecticide because corn borer and armyworm show up some summers.

My whole budget is tight — spending more on fertilizer means less for other things — but going hungry is worse than wasting a few kilos of urea. I expect wheat around 520 kg per mu and maize around 580 kg per mu. That is enough for my household of three and some to sell.
